questions.rawText:
A regular pentagon has its vertices on a circle. From vertex A four forces are applied towards the
other four vertices with magnitudes 6 kN, 8 kN, 8 kN, and 6 kN, respectively as shown in the figure.
Determine the resultant force.

Determine the force P required to impend motion of 1000 kN block upwards. Consider the
coefficient of limiting friction as 0.25 for all contact surfaces. Neglect the weight of the wedge.

Explain how access control and fire alarm systems together contribute to building safety and
occupant security in a smart building environment.

Determine the magnitude of load P required to establish the condition under which there is no net
change in the total length of the bar ABCD shown in the figure. Assume E = 200 GPa.

Derive an expression for elongation of a tapered bar of rectangular cross-section subjected to an
axial tensile load "W". The bar has varying depths from d1 to d2 (d1 < d2) and uniform thickness 't'
over length L.

An aluminium block of size 300 mm (length) x 100 mm (width) x 50 mm (height) is subjected to a
tensile force of 150 kN along its length and a compressive force of 200 kN along its width.
Determine the change in its length, width, and height. Assume the modulus of elasticity (E) for
aluminium as 70 GPa and Poisson's ratio as 0.33.

A circular bar ABCD, 3m long is subjected to a tensile force of 60kN as shown in the figure. If the
stress in the middle portion BC is not to exceed 175 MPa, then what should be its diameter? Also
find the length of the middle portion, if the total extension of the bar should not exceed by 3.25 mm.
Take E as 100 GPa.

Compute the shearing stress in the pin/hinge at B for the member supported as shown in Figure.
The pin/hinge diameter is 20 mm.
Explain is the necessity of instrument calibration? List any six key factors.

Explain working Mechanism of
i) Force Transducer.
ii) Distance sensor.

questions.rawText:
The forces 20 N, 30 N, 40 N, 50 N and 60 N are acting at one of the angular points of a regular
hexagon, towards the other five angular points, taken in order. Find the magnitude and direction of
the resultant force.

A light string ABCDE whose extremity A is fixed, has weights W1 and W2 attached to it at B and C.
It passes round a small frictionless pulley (neglect the weight of pulley) at D carrying a weight of 300
N at the free end E as shown in the figure. If in the equilibrium position, BC is horizontal, find
(i) Tension in the portions AB, BC and CD of the string and
(ii) Magnitudes of W1 and W2.

Explain the Energy Efficiency Ratio (EER) and the Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio (SEER)
highlighting the differences between their operating conditions.

Calculate the stress developed in each section of the composite bar consisting of steel, aluminum, and
bronze sections rigidly connected as shown in the figure. Also, determine the deformation of each section
and the overall change in length of the bar.
Given:
Ebronze = 100 GPa, Ealuminium = 70 GPa, Esteel = 200 GPa.
Cross sectional area and length of Aluminum section: 600 mm2 and 800 mm respectively.
Cross sectional area and length of Steel section: 1000 mm2 and 1200 mm respectively.
Cross sectional area and length of Bronze section: 1500 mm2 and 1400 mm respectively.

A steel bar 40 mm × 40 mm in cross-section and 140 mm length is subjected to an axial
compressive load of 250 kN longitudinally.
i) Determine the deformation in length of the bar if the lateral strain is fully prevented.
ii) Determine the deformation in length of the bar if only one-third of the lateral strain is prevented.
Take Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio of steel bar as 205 GPa and 0.3 respectively.

Derive the relationship between young's modulus (E) and modulus of rigidity (G) for a deformable
body.

A mild steel bar of 30 mm diameter, 250 mm length, has an extension of 0.20 mm under a load of
85 kN. The load at the elastic limit is 170 kN, and the ultimate load is 280 kN. The total extension is
45 mm and diameter at the fracture is 19.5 mm. Calculate the elastic modulus of the material, stress
at the elastic limit, ultimate strength of the material, percentage elongation and percentage
reduction in cross-sectional area.

A bar 25 mm in diameter and 500 mm in length is acted upon by an axial load of 40 kN. The
elongation of the bar and change in diameter are measured as 0.175 mm and 0.0041 mm,
respectively. Calculate Poisson's ratio and three moduli. Also, determine the allowable stress if a
factor of safety is 1.5.
Explain briefly five types of displacement sensors.

Explain the working mechanisms of
i) Strain gauge
ii) pH sensor
